incumbent.text: Hypothesis: a real multiline private-key block survives because the PEM regex expects literal backslash-n separators and only a generic header. Applicability: the central formatter is attached to file logging, and the analyst may call it directly on a disposable string. Bounded test: emit generic, RSA, and ENCRYPTED blocks with real newlines and a base64 marker, plus a literal-backslash-n control. Expected result: base64 markers disappear and END headers remain; falsifier: any marker survives. Cleanup: delete the temporary log and fixture key material.

hint: A Python connector's central formatter now has a generalized private-key span plus key-name authentication-code, authorization-scheme, and double-quoted cloud-key maskers. A 23-carrier pristine/patched matrix passed with benign controls, but the change has not been exported as a standalone diff, applied to a fresh copy, or checked against the repository's existing secret-detector test functions. Question: does the patch replay cleanly and preserve existing behavior and benign PEM-adjacent text?
